ASSESSMENT AND PLAN: 1. Encounter for Medicare annual wellness exam (Primary) 2. Atherosclerosis of aorta (HCC) 3. Pulmonary hypertension (HCC) 4. Central sleep apnea 5. OSA (obstructive sleep apnea) 6. Chronic bilateral low back pain with bilateral sciatica 7. Long term current use of opiate analgesic 8. Pure hypercholesterolemia 9. Essential hypertension 10. Diastolic dysfunction 11. Coronary artery calcification seen on CT scan 12. Cerebral microvascular disease 13. Bilateral carotid artery stenosis 14. Generalized anxiety disorder 15. Age-related osteoporosis without current pathological fracture 16. Depression screening negative [Z13.31] 17. Encounter for risk and functional assessment of patient 18. At risk for falls 19. BMI 29.0-29.9,adult 20. Dietary counseling 21. Exercise counseling Colon cancer screening is up to date. Repeat not needed due to age.Breast cancer screening is up to date. CT abdomen done 12/21/2019 showed atherosclerotic disease involving abdominal aorta without aneurysm. Continue aspirin and statin. ECHO done 7/19/202 showed RVSP measured 51 mmHg. This was done in the setting of acute PE. I discussed repeating ECHO to re-evaluate pulmonary pressure but Sylvia defers at this time, as it would not change current treatment.Shortly after that, she was evaluated by Sleep Medicine. Sleep study done 8/16/2022 was positive for sleep apnea with AHI 53.3. Repeat study with CPAP done 9/23/2022 and revealed central sleep apnea. Now Sylvia is using and benefiting from BiPAP. Sylvia continues to complain of chronic low back pain. MRI lumbar spine done 10/11/2023 showed advanced neural foraminal narrowing bilaterally, right greater than left, at L1-2. Mild to moderate neural foraminal narrowing bilaterally at L2-3. Also showed disc bulge present with moderate facet arthropathy and prominence of ligamentum flavum contributing to moderate to severe spinal canal narrowing at L1-2 and L2-3. Surgery has been discussed but Sylvia does not want to do that. She will continue treatment with Pain Medicine. They prescribe her Norco and Gabapentin. Continue Atorvastatin. Blood pressure appears controlled, continue present management. ECHO done 7/22/2022 showed grade I/IV mild diastolic dysfunction. This was done in the setting of acute PE. She does not have any signs or symptoms of heart failure. She is euvolemic on exam without diuretic. CT abdomen done 12/21/2019 showed coronary artery calcifications and again on CTA thorax done 7/22/2022. Continue aspirin and statin. MRI brain done 9/29/2017 showed chronic small vessel ischemic disease. Continue blood pressure control, aspirin, statin. CTA neck done 9/29/2017 showed both calcified and noncalcified plaque at the carotid bifurcation and carotid bulb bilaterally. The degree of luminal narrowing is estimated to be less than 50%. Continue statin and aspirin. Sylvia admits to having more anxiety recently due to husband getting tested for dementia. She does not want to change her current dose of citalopram. Forteo 2009-2011, Prolia 2011-2016, Started Evista in 2020, which was stopped in 7/2022 due to patient having bilateral PE. Started Reclast in 2023. Continue management with Tammy Beckett NP. Patient's fall risk was assessed today. See under HPI. She is at risk for falls due to the pain medication she takes. She has had osteoporotic fractures and is at risk for another fracture. Safety precautions discussed. I counseled patient on benefits of regular exercise and making healthy diet choices. Return in about 6 months (around 6/4/2024) for Med review.
